obligation: Card brand notice: Visa account data compromise
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised, Visa Supplemental Requirements v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Section A.1 to A.4
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa payment account data or to a system that stores, processes, or transmits it, on either platform
deadline: Report to Visa within 3 calendar days of suspicion or confirmation; incident report within 3 calendar days after notifying Visa; at-risk account numbers within 3 calendar days of discovery, of Visa's request, or of setting the window of exposure
notify: Visa Global Risk Investigations (through the acquiring sponsor bank and Visa's Global Investigations Management Tool); acquiring bank immediately
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the company stores, processes, and transmits Visa account data as a third-party processor for both sponsor banks. Other brands: follow each brand's rules through the sponsor banks (timing not verified here)

obligation: Sponsor bank notice of suspected account data compromise
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.3; sponsor agreements with Bank A and Bank B (contract)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed account data compromise affecting a bank's program
deadline: Immediately (Visa); within 24 hours under each sponsor agreement
notify: The affected sponsor bank's designated security and compliance contacts (Bank B for Integrated Payments merchants; Bank A for core merchants)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

trigger: Computer-security incident that has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to materially disrupt or degrade, covered services to Bank A for four or more hours. Covered services: clearing, settlement, reconciliation, and merchant funding files (sponsor agreement; 12 U.S.C. 1867(c)). Excludes previously communicated maintenance, testing, or updates (53.4(b))
deadline: As soon as possible after the determination
notify: At least one bank-designated point of contact; if none on file, Bank A's CEO and CIO or two individuals of comparable responsibility (53.4(a)(2))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - bank service provider to Bank A (OCC-supervised national bank). Card data theft alone does not trigger it; disruption of covered services for 4 or more hours does

trigger: Same trigger as 53.4 for covered services to Bank B
deadline: As soon as possible after the determination
notify: At least one bank-designated point of contact; if none on file, Bank B's CEO and CIO or two individuals of comparable responsibility (304.24(a)(2))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - bank service provider to Bank B (FDIC-supervised insured state nonmember bank) since 2025-10-01. Bank B's designated contacts are not yet on file (POAM-017)

trigger: Same trigger for Board-supervised banking organization customers
deadline: As soon as possible
notify: Bank-designated points of contact
applies_at_this_tier: No - no services are performed for a Board-supervised banking organization

obligation: Banking organization notification incident (sponsor banks' own duty)
trigger: Notification incident at the banking organization
deadline: No later than 36 hours after the bank determines a notification incident occurred
notify: The bank's primary federal regulator (by the bank)
applies_at_this_tier: No - applies to the sponsor banks, not the company. The company's prompt notice gives each bank what it needs for its own decision

trigger: Acquisition of unencrypted customer information without the individual's authorization (unauthorized access presumed to be acquisition absent reliable evidence otherwise) involving the information of at least 500 consumers
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery (first day known to any employee, officer, or agent other than the person committing the breach)
notify: Federal Trade Commission, through the electronic form on ftc.gov
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - financial institution under 16 CFR 314. The company counts affected cardholders toward the 500 (conservative reading; confirm with counsel)

trigger: A law enforcement official provides a written determination that public notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: Initial delay of up to 30 days after notice to the FTC; up to 60 more days on written request; further delay only if FTC staff agrees
notify: Include in the FTC notice; the FTC contacts the official
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Third-party agent notice to merchants (Florida worked example)
trigger: Breach of security of a system the company maintains for merchants (covered entities) involving personal information of Florida residents (name plus card number with any required security code)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
notify: Each affected merchant, with all information it needs for its own notices; for Integrated Payments merchants, directly or through their ISV
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the company is a third-party agent for its merchants' cardholder data

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (covered entity duty)
trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents where the company is the covered entity (for example merchant owner data), or when sending notices for a merchant
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (15 more days with good cause given in writing to the department within 30 days)
notify: Affected Florida residents
applies_at_this_tier: Yes when the company owns the data or sends notices for a merchant

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (the good-cause extension does not apply to this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents and the company is the covered entity (otherwise the merchant's duty)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000 individuals are notified

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents; definitions and third-party agent rules vary
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Merchants (as data owners); residents; state attorneys general or regulators where required
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - merchants in all 50 states; apply the law of each state where affected residents live

trigger: Security incident affecting merchant or cardholder data, or delayed funding
deadline: Per each agreement
notify: Affected merchants and ISV partners
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved; presumption of denial); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if an extortion demand is made

trigger: Criminal compromise of payment data or ransomware
deadline: As soon as practicable; coordinate with counsel and the PFI
notify: U.S. Secret Service field office; FBI field office or IC3
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the breach hotline before hiring vendors
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

trigger: Severity 1 incident
deadline: Within 4 hours of declaration (company protocol)
notify: Audit committee chair; PE sponsor operating partner
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - internal governance

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours (ransom payment). Not yet effective
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25. Under the proposed size criterion (exceeds the SBA size standard) the company would likely be covered; recheck when final

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident
citation: Form 8-K Item 1.05; Regulation S-K Item 106 (17 CFR 229.106) for annual disclosure
trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at an SEC registrant
deadline: Within 4 business days after determining materiality
notify: SEC (public filing)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is privately held and not an SEC registrant

trigger: SCI event at an SCI entity
deadline: Immediately; written notice within 24 hours
notify: SEC
applies_at_this_tier: No - not an SCI entity

trigger: Reportable cyber incident at a federally insured credit union
deadline: No later than 72 hours
notify: NCUA
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a credit union and serves none

trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
